name: The Hundred
description: A breath-driven warm-up that engages the abdominals while pumping the arms and stabilizing the ribcage.

benefits: Improves lung capacity and steady core support through intentional breath pacing.
setup: Lie supine with knees bent in tabletop, shoulders relaxed, and arms long by your sides.
breathing: Inhale for five pumps, exhale for five pumps; keep the ribs long and shoulders relaxed.
safetyNote: Maintain even breathing, keep the spine supported, and stop if any sharp pain or breath-holding occurs.
whereToFeel: Feel the work in the abdominals and inner thighs as you stabilize the ribcage.

transitionOut: Lower the head and feet to the mat, then roll to your side to sit up safely.
selfCheck: Check: Are your abdominals engaged and your neck relaxed?
whatToAvoid: Avoid poking the chin forward, allowing the lower back to arch off the mat, or holding the breath during the arm pumps.
instructorNote: Watch for rib-popping on the inhale and premature shoulder tension. Keep beginners head-down and progress to head-float only once the pelvis is truly stable.
teachingCues: Lower back heavy and long.
Pump from the shoulders, not the wrists.
Breathe into the back of your ribs.
instructions: Lie supine with knees bent in tabletop, shoulders relaxed, and arms long by your sides.
Lift your head, neck and shoulders off the mat while keeping the lower back grounded.
Pump your arms vigorously in small motions alongside the body.
Coordinate the movement with breath: inhale for five pumps, exhale for five pumps.
Stay steady through the ribs and avoid pressing the shoulders into the ears.
Regression: Keep the head on the mat and legs lower to reduce cervical strain and core load. Progression: Extend the legs higher while keeping the pelvis stable.
modifications: Keep the head on the mat and legs lower to reduce cervical strain and core load.

For immunosuppression, recent recovery, or sensitive skin, choose clean props, gentle regressions, and avoid direct pressure on irritated areas.
progressions: Extend the legs higher while keeping the pelvis stable.
Increase arm speed slightly once breath coordination is steady.
commonMistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch away from the mat.
Tensing the shoulders or lifting them toward the ears.
